0xcafed00d-taptool-readme-md.text:
# taptool

`taptool` is a Go command line utility for ZX Spectrum `.tap` tape archives.

It can:

- analyze TAP records, offsets, flags, headers, and checksums
- extract useful files from a TAP archive: `.bas`, `.bin`, and `manifest.json`
- assemble a TAP archive from a BASIC loader and CODE blocks
- append a BASIC loader or CODE blocks to an existing TAP archive

## Build

```sh
go build ./cmd/taptool
./taptool version
```

Release builds for the current Linux, macOS, and Windows target matrix can be
created with:

```sh
./scripts/build.sh
```

Build artifacts are written under `dist/`. The script embeds the version,
commit, and build date into each binary. The default version is `0.1.0`; set
`VERSION` to override it:

```sh
VERSION=0.2.0 ./scripts/build.sh
PLATFORMS="linux/amd64 windows/amd64" ./scripts/build.sh
```

## Commands

```sh
taptool version
taptool --version

taptool analyze example_taps/nohzdyve.tap
taptool analyze --json example_taps/nohzdyve.tap

taptool extract -o extracted example_taps/nohzdyve.tap

taptool assemble -o game.tap --loader examples/loader.bas --block game.bin:32768:GAME

taptool assemble -o game128.tap \
  --loader examples/loader128.bas \
  --block bank3.bin:49152:BANK3 \
  --block bank4.bin:49152:BANK4 \
  --block main.bin:32768:MAIN

taptool append --block bank5.bin:49152:BANK5 game128.tap
```

## Extract

`extract` writes these outputs:

- `.bas` files for BASIC Program blocks
- `.bin` files for CODE/array blocks and unpaired data records
- `manifest.json` with record metadata

Example:

```sh
taptool extract -o extracted example_taps/nohzdyve.tap
```

For a BASIC loader, extraction may produce files such as:

```text
0000_program_LOADER.bas
manifest.json
```

The `.bas` file is detokenized text BASIC.

For a loader followed by CODE blocks, extraction may produce files such as:

```text
0000_program_LOADER.bas
0002_code_BANK3.bin
0004_code_MAIN.bin
manifest.json
```

The `.bin` files contain the actual bytes loaded by the Spectrum, with TAP
length fields, flag bytes, checksums, and header records removed. The manifest
keeps the full per-record metadata, including headers, offsets, flags, and
checksums.

## Assemble

`assemble` creates a new TAP archive from generated records only. It accepts:

- `--loader LOADER.bas`
- repeated `--block FILE[:START[:NAME]]`

The loader is written first as a BASIC Program header/data pair. Each `--block`
is written after that as a normal CODE header/data pair, in command-line order.

```sh
taptool assemble -o game.tap --loader examples/loader.bas --block game.bin:32768:GAME
```

`--block` fields:

```text
FILE              binary file to load
START             optional load address, default 32768
NAME              optional Spectrum tape name, default derived from filename
```

Examples:

```sh
taptool assemble -o banks.tap --block bank3.bin:49152:BANK3 --block bank4.bin:49152:BANK4
taptool assemble -o main.tap --block main.bin
taptool assemble -o named.tap --block main.bin::MAIN
```

## Append

`append` adds generated records to the end of an existing TAP archive in place.
It validates the existing TAP before writing.

```sh
taptool append --block bank5.bin:49152:BANK5 game128.tap
taptool append --loader examples/loader.bas game.tap
```

`append` uses the same `--loader` and `--block` meanings as `assemble`.

## TAP Format

A `.tap` archive is a plain sequence of length-prefixed records. It does not
store tape timing, pauses, turbo-loader pulses, or hardware metadata. For those
details you usually need a richer format such as `.tzx`.

Each TAP record has this outer structure:

```text
2-byte little-endian payload length
payload bytes
```

The length is the number of payload bytes only. It does not include the two
length bytes themselves. Records appear back-to-back until the end of the file:

```text
[length][payload][length][payload][length][payload]...
```

The payload normally contains:

```text
flag byte + data bytes + checksum byte
```

The checksum is the XOR of every payload byte except the checksum byte itself.
Header blocks have flag `0x00` and a 19-byte payload. Data blocks commonly use
flag `0xff`.

### Header Payloads

A standard Spectrum header payload is 19 bytes:

```text
byte 0       flag byte, usually 0x00 for a header
byte 1       block type
bytes 2-11   filename, padded with spaces to 10 bytes
bytes 12-13  data length, little-endian
bytes 14-15  parameter 1, little-endian
bytes 16-17  parameter 2, little-endian
byte 18      checksum
```

Block type values:

```text
0  BASIC Program
1  Number array
2  Character array
3  CODE / bytes
```

For BASIC Program headers, parameter 1 is the autostart line, or `32768` for no
autostart. Parameter 2 is usually the program length. For CODE headers,
parameter 1 is the load address. This tool writes parameter 2 as `32768` for
CODE blocks, matching common Spectrum TAP conventions.

### Data Payloads

A standard data payload is:

```text
0xff + raw loaded bytes + checksum
```

For CODE/array blocks, the raw loaded bytes are what `extract` writes to `.bin`
files. For a CODE block, those are the exact bytes that `LOAD "" CODE` places
in memory. For a BASIC Program block, those bytes are tokenized BASIC, which
`extract` detokenizes into a `.bas` file instead.

### Checksums

The checksum is a simple XOR:

```text
checksum = flag XOR data[0] XOR data[1] XOR ... XOR data[n]
```

When a TAP record is valid, XORing every byte in the payload, including the
stored checksum byte, gives `0x00`.

## BASIC Loaders

`taptool` can compile a numbered text BASIC loader when you pass it with
`--loader`.

Example `examples/loader.bas`:

```basic
10 CLEAR 32767
20 LOAD "" CODE
30 RANDOMIZE USR 32768
```

`CLEAR 32767` lowers `RAMTOP`, which is the highest address BASIC is allowed to
use. This also moves the BASIC/GOSUB stack area and the Z80 machine stack below
that limit, with the stack growing downwards. For a loader, that keeps BASIC and
the stack away from machine code loaded at `32768` and above.

The tokenizer is intentionally small. It supports the keywords needed for
typical loaders, including `CLEAR`, `LOAD`, `CODE`, `RANDOMIZE`, `USR`, `REM`,
`PRINT`, `POKE`, `OUT`, `PAUSE`, `BORDER`, `INK`, `PAPER`, `FLASH`, and
`BRIGHT`, plus non-negative integer constants from `0` to `65535`.

To create a complete tape with a BASIC loader followed by a CODE block:

```sh
taptool assemble -o game.tap --loader examples/loader.bas --block game.bin:32768:GAME
```

A loader line such as `LOAD "" CODE` will load the following CODE block using
the address saved in its header, and `RANDOMIZE USR 32768` will execute it.

## 128K Bank Loaders

Spectrum 128K machines use the same ordinary BASIC token encoding and the same
standard TAP block structure for ROM-style tape loads. 128 BASIC adds extra
features and commands, but loader statements such as `LOAD`, `CODE`, `POKE`,
`OUT`, and `RANDOMIZE USR` use the normal token bytes.

The `CLEAR 32767` line in `examples/loader128.bas` is deliberately conservative:
it keeps BASIC and the stack below `32768`, leaving both the main code area and
the `49152..65535` switchable bank window clear for loaded blocks.

The hardware paging port is `32765` (`0x7ffd`). The system variable at `23388`
keeps a copy of the last value written to that port, so a BASIC loader should
update it before paging:

```basic
20 LET b=16+3: POKE 23388,b: OUT 32765,b: LOAD "" CODE 49152
30 LET b=16+4: POKE 23388,b: OUT 32765,b: LOAD "" CODE 49152
40 LET b=16+0: POKE 23388,b: OUT 32765,b
```

See `examples/loader128.bas` for a full template. Each `LOAD "" CODE 49152`
loads the next CODE block into the currently paged 16K RAM bank at
`49152..65535`. Build the complete tape with repeated `--block` options in the
same order as the loader reads them.

# amigamand

**A Mandelbrot and Julia set explorer for the Amiga.** It runs on AmigaOS 3.1 (68020 and up), draws in 256 colours on an AGA
machine (Amiga 1200, 4000), zooms with the mouse, is scriptable from ARexx, and saves its pictures as IFF ILBM.

![Four pictures drawn by amigamand itself: the whole Mandelbrot set, a spiral in Fire colours, a Julia set and a seahorse valley](docs/gallery.png)

*All four pictures were drawn by amigamand (hires, 256 colours) and saved as ILBM by its own `SAVE` option.*

- **Mandelbrot and Julia sets**, 1 to 255 iterations, five palettes with colour cycling
- **AGA**: 256 colours, hires and interlace; falls back to fewer colours by itself on OCS/ECS; PAL and NTSC
- **Two programs**: `amigamand` (fixed point, runs on any 68020) and `amigamand-fpu` (68881/68882/68040+, deeper zoom)
- **ARexx port** `AMIGAMAND`, **IFF ILBM** saving, ASL file and screen mode requesters, Workbench icon with tool types
- **Fast**: the pixel loop is hand-written 68020 assembly, the screen is written bitplane by bitplane by its own
  chunky-to-planar routine, and symmetry and region filling skip work that is not needed
- **Tested**: a 15-test suite drives the real programs in an emulator and checks the pictures pixel for pixel

## Quick start

The two programs, `amigamand` and `amigamand-fpu`, and their icons are in the repository, ready to copy to an Amiga or a disk
image. To try them on a Mac with [FS-UAE](https://fs-uae.net):

    git clone https://github.com/Shadester/amigamand && cd amigamand
    ./run                 # starts amigamand in an emulated A1200

`./run` needs FS-UAE, and your own Kickstart 3.1 A1200 ROM and Workbench 3.1 disk image in `~/Documents/FS-UAE` (they are not
part of this repository). `./run MODE 0 ITER 255` passes start options, `./run fpu JULIA` runs the FPU build.
`tools/setup.sh check` says what is missing.

## Using it

**Mouse.** Left click centres the view on that point. Left drag draws a box and zooms into it. The right button opens the menu
(the Right-Amiga shortcuts work too).

**Keys.**

| key | does |
|---|---|
| `+` `-` | zoom in, out |
| cursor keys | pan a quarter of the picture |
| `0` | reset the view |
| `j` | the Julia set of the point you clicked last |
| `m` | back to the Mandelbrot set |
| `r` | redraw |
| `s` | save as ILBM (opens a file requester) |
| `c` | cycle the colours |
| space | stop a render |
| Esc | quit |

**Menu.** *Project*: redraw, abort, save, quit. *View*: zoom, reset, Mandelbrot, Julia. *Mode*: lores, hires, hires interlace, or
"Other..." for any screen mode the machine has. *Palette*: Rainbow, Fire, Ocean, Gray, Electric, and cycle colours. *Detail*: 64,
128 or 255 iterations, and fast fill.

A picture is drawn coarse first, then refined, so you see where you are going before it is finished.

### Start options

From a Shell, or as tool types in the icon (the icon has them ready; those in brackets are switched off):

    amigamand [MODE n] [CX x] [CY y] [SPAN s] [ITER n] [PALETTE name] [JULIA] [JR x] [JI y]
              [SAVE file] [QUIT] [EXACT] [DEPTH n]

| option | meaning |
|---|---|
| `MODE` | 0 lores, 1 hires (default), 2 hires interlace. 320x256, 640x256, 640x512 on PAL; 200 and 400 lines on NTSC |
| `CX CY SPAN` | the centre of the view and its width, for example `CX -0.7436 CY 0.1318 SPAN 0.02` |
| `ITER` | at most this many iterations, 1 to 255 (default 128) |
| `PALETTE` | `Rainbow`, `Fire`, `Ocean`, `Gray`, `Electric`, or 0 to 4 |
| `JULIA`, `JR`, `JI` | show the Julia set of the constant JR + JI i (default -0.8 + 0.156i) |
| `SAVE`, `QUIT` | save an ILBM when the first picture is finished, and quit |
| `EXACT` | no fast fill (see *How it is fast*) |
| `DEPTH` | bitplanes, 1 to 8. Fewer planes: fewer colours, less video DMA, faster on a stock A1200 |

`SAVE` and `QUIT` make it a batch tool:

    amigamand MODE 1 CX -0.7453 CY 0.1127 SPAN 0.006 ITER 255 PALETTE Ocean SAVE RAM:sea.iff QUIT

### ARexx

The port is `AMIGAMAND`:

    /* zoom into the spiral and save it */
    options results
    address AMIGAMAND
    'ITER 255'
    'PALETTE fire'
    'ZOOM -0.7436 0.1318 0.02'
    'WAIT'                      /* returns when the picture is finished */
    'SAVE RAM:spiral.iff'
    'QUERY'                     /* the view, as a result string */
    say result
    'QUIT'

| command | |
|---|---|
| `RENDER`, `ABORT`, `WAIT`, `RESET` | draw again, stop, wait until finished, default view |
| `ZOOM cx cy span`, `CENTER x y`, `SPAN s` | set the view |
| `MODE n`, `ITER n`, `PALETTE name\|n`, `CYCLE ON\|OFF`, `FAST ON\|OFF` | settings |
| `JULIA [re im]`, `MANDELBROT` | which set |
| `SAVE file` | write an ILBM |
| `QUERY` | returns `MANDELBROT cx cy span iterations WxHxplanes palette DONE ticks` (or `RENDERING`) |
| `QUIT` | |

An unknown command or a bad argument returns 10.

### Saved pictures

ILBM with the real palette, ByteRun1 packing, and the screen mode ID in `CAMG`, so a viewer opens it in the mode it was drawn in.

## Building

You need a C compiler for the host and the Amiga cross compiler vbcc with vasm, vlink and the NDK headers. `tools/setup.sh`
downloads and builds them into `toolchain/` inside the repository (about two minutes, nothing is installed elsewhere), and
checks every download against a SHA-256:

    tools/setup.sh        # needs cc, make, curl, tar and lha (macOS: brew install lhasa)
    make                  # amigamand and amigamand-fpu

The programs are committed, and a rebuild gives the same bytes.

`tools/make_icon.py` writes the two `.info` files. `tools/run.sh` boots a whole Workbench in FS-UAE with the programs and icons
on a volume `AMIGAMAND:`. `CPU=68020 FPU= ./run` is a stock A1200; the default is a 68040, the fastest emulated machine that
makes a difference.

## Tests

    tools/test/test.sh

takes about ten minutes and boots the real programs in FS-UAE. It checks the pens of five views against stored hashes, that
fast fill and the periodicity check draw what plain iteration draws, the interlace, NTSC and 5-plane modes, the FPU build (and
its clean exit without an FPU), keys, menu shortcuts, colour cycling, abort, both ASL requesters, saving, the mouse handlers,
the icon (loaded by the real `icon.library`), the Workbench tool types and the real ARexx. `tools/test/README.md` has the list.

## How it is fast

Ticks of 1/50 s for one picture on an emulated stock A1200 (68020, no fast RAM), against the first working version:

| picture | first | now |
|---|---|---|
| the whole set, hires, 128 iterations | 1309 (26 s) | 680 (14 s) |
| the spiral, lores, 255 iterations | 6964 (139 s) | 3953 (79 s) |
| a Julia set, hires | 3496 (70 s) | 1160 (23 s) |

On an accelerated machine, or in FS-UAE with a 68040, the same pictures take a second or two. What made the difference, in the
order it paid:

- **Own chunky-to-planar conversion** straight into the screen's bitplanes. graphics.library's `WriteChunkyPixels` is a generic
  routine on AGA and cost 30% of a frame on a 68020, and most of the time on faster CPUs.
- **The whole pixel loop in assembly**, one call for each row, with z and c in Q4.28 and the high long of `muls.l` giving the
  squares directly. A call for every pixel cost more than the few iterations most pixels need.
- **Symmetry.** The set is mirrored about the real axis; every Julia set is the same turned half way round. Half the work.
- **Skipping the obvious.** Points outside radius 2, and inside the main cardioid and the period-2 bulb, are known without iterating.
- **Fast fill** (Mariani-Silver) when zoomed in: if the border of a rectangle is one colour, so is its inside. And a **periodicity
  check** that stops iterating an orbit that has come back to itself. Both switch themselves off where they do not pay.

`CLAUDE.md` has the full account, including what was tried and did not work (an exact periodicity check cannot fire in fixed
point; a cheaper two-multiply loop cannot give the same pictures).

On a stock A1200 the CPU shares chip RAM with the video DMA: a 256-colour hires screen is about 40% slower than the same work
with 2 bitplanes (`DEPTH 2`). Any fast RAM removes that.

## Limits

- Fixed point has 24 bits of fraction, so below a span of about 1e-4 the picture turns blocky. Use `amigamand-fpu`.
- Fast fill and the periodicity check are heuristics (a region is taken to be one colour when its border is, an orbit to be
  periodic when it returns close to itself). They matched plain iteration pixel for pixel in every test; `EXACT` switches the fill off.
- Developed and tested in FS-UAE only. The mouse itself, the buttons of the screen mode requester and the icon on a real
  Workbench could not be tried; nobody has run it on a real Amiga yet.

## Layout

| file | |
|---|---|
| `main.c` | the user interface, rendering control, requesters, ARexx commands, start options |
| `view.c`, `view.h` | the view, the number type (Q8.24 or `double`), the loops |
| `iter020.s` | the fixed-point pixel loop |
| `c2p.c` | chunky to planar |
| `palette.c`, `ilbm.c`, `rexx.c` | palettes, IFF ILBM writer, the ARexx port |
| `run`, `tools/` | the run script, setup, icon generator, the test suite |

## Licence

MIT, see `LICENSE`. That covers the source, the programs, the icons and the pictures in this repository.

The Amiga cross compiler (vbcc, vasm, vlink) and the NDK headers that `tools/setup.sh` downloads are not part of it and have
their own terms, as do your Kickstart ROM and Workbench disk, which this repository neither contains nor needs to contain.

# DitherExtend

[![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/Generated-Documentation-yellow)](https://dpt.github.io/Module.DitherExt/)

A reverse engineering of the RISC OS module `DitherExtend` 0.60 (13 Nov 2002, Computer Concepts Ltd), together with a C port of it.

DitherExtend provides halftone and colour pattern dithering, antialias blending and related colour conversion SWIs. Its SWI chunk is `&44580`.

## Contents

| Path              | What it is                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Asm/DitherExt.s` | Annotated objasm disassembly with meaningful labels. Assembles byte-identical to the original module. |
| `C/`              | CMHG module in C, ported routine by routine from the disassembly.                                     |
| `prminxml/`       | Interface documentation in PRM-in-XML, published to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/pages.yml`.    |

The original module binary is not part of this repository, as it is copyrighted. To verify the disassembly, assemble `Asm/DitherExt.s` and compare the output with your own copy of `DitherExt,ffa` (`DitherExtend` 0.60, `&6F1C` bytes).

## SWIs

The module owns SWI chunk `&44580` (`DitherExtend_`). It reimplements the RISC OS ColourTrans SWIs that choose colours for a screen mode (`ColourTrans_SelectTable`, `ColourTrans_ReturnGCOL` and so on), adding dithering. SWI offsets `0` to `&D` have the same names and the same order as the matching ColourTrans SWIs. While dithering is enabled and not suspended, the module also takes these calls from ColourV and passes them on, so ColourTrans callers get dithered colours without change. The other SWIs are extensions.

The register lists below come from the disassembly and the C port. Colours are `&BBGGRR00` words. A mode argument is a mode number or a mode selector. A palette argument of `0` means the default palette for the mode and `-1` means the current palette. A colour number is the pixel value that selects a colour in the mode, while a GCOL value is the number that the `GCOL` command takes for the same colour, which differs from the colour number in some modes (such as 256 colour modes).

| Offset | SWI                            | Description                                                                                      | Entry                                                                                           | Exit                                        |
| ------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `&00`  | `SelectTable`                  | Build a table mapping each colour of the source mode to a colour number in the destination mode. | R0 source mode, R1 source palette, R2 destination mode, R3 destination palette, R4 table buffer | Table written to R4                         |
| `&01`  | `SelectGCOLTable`              | As `SelectTable`, but the entries are GCOL values.                                               | As `SelectTable`                                                                                | Entries are GCOL values in 256 colour modes |
| `&02`  | `ReturnGCOL`                   | Return the GCOL value that best matches a colour in the current mode.                            | R0 colour                                                                                       | R0 GCOL value                               |
| `&03`  | `SetGCOL`                      | Set the graphics foreground or background colour, building a dither pattern when needed.         | R0 colour, R3 flags (bit 7 picks the buffer half), R4 mask row (low 3 bits)                     | R0 GCOL value; pattern built                |
| `&04`  | `ReturnColourNumber`           | Return the colour number that best matches a colour in the current mode.                         | R0 colour                                                                                       | R0 colour number                            |
| `&05`  | `ReturnGCOLForMode`            | As `ReturnGCOL`, for a given mode and palette.                                                   | R0 colour, R1 mode, R2 palette                                                                  | R0 GCOL value                               |
| `&06`  | `ReturnColourNumberForMode`    | As `ReturnColourNumber`, for a given mode and palette.                                           | R0 colour, R1 mode, R2 palette                                                                  | R0 colour number                            |
| `&07`  | `ReturnOppGCOL`                | Return the GCOL value of the colour most contrasting with a colour.                              | R0 colour                                                                                       | R0 GCOL value                               |
| `&08`  | `SetOppGCOL`                   | As `SetGCOL`, using the contrasting colour.                                                      | As `SetGCOL`                                                                                    | As `SetGCOL`                                |
| `&09`  | `ReturnOppColourNumber`        | Return the colour number of the colour most contrasting with a colour.                           | R0 colour                                                                                       | R0 colour number                            |
| `&0A`  | `ReturnOppGCOLForMode`         | As `ReturnOppGCOL`, for a given mode and palette.                                                | As `ReturnGCOLForMode`                                                                          | R0 GCOL value                               |
| `&0B`  | `ReturnOppColourNumberForMode` | As `ReturnOppColourNumber`, for a given mode and palette.                                        | As `ReturnColourNumberForMode`                                                                  | R0 colour number                            |
| `&0C`  | `GCOLToColourNumber`           | Convert a GCOL value to a colour number.                                                         | R0 GCOL value                                                                                   | R0 colour number                            |
| `&0D`  | `ColourNumberToGCOL`           | Convert a colour number to a GCOL value.                                                         | R0 colour number                                                                                | R0 GCOL value                               |
| `&0E`  | `Info`                         | Read the module flags.                                                                           |                                                                                                 | R0 flags                                    |
| `&0F`  | `Control`                      | Change the module control bits.                                                                  | R0 EOR mask, R1 AND mask (control bits only)                                                    | R0 new flags                                |
| `&10`  | `ReturnColourPattern`          | Build the 32 byte dither pattern for a colour.                                                   | R0 colour, R2 buffer (32 bytes)                                                                 | Pattern written                             |
| `&11`  | `ReturnColourPatternTable`     | Build dither patterns for a range of colours.                                                    | R0 first colour, R1 last colour, R2 buffer (256 patterns of 32 bytes)                           | Patterns written                            |
| `&12`  | `InvalidatePalette`            | Free the cached palette data. Call after the palette changes.                                    |                                                                                                 | Palette caches freed                        |
| `&13`  | `Antialias`                    | Get the workspace and the blend routine for the current screen depth.                            |                                                                                                 | R0 workspace, R1 blend routine (see below)  |
| `&14`  | `ReadPalette`                  | Read the palette of a mode into a buffer.                                                        | R0 mode, R1 palette, R2 buffer                                                                  | Palette words written                       |
| `&15`  | `ReturnColourPatternArray`     | Build and return the block of patterns for every colour.                                         |                                                                                                 | R0 block of `&20000` bytes                  |
| `&16`  | `SetHalftone`                  | Set the halftone screen.                                                                         | R0 to R7 halftone description                                                                   |                                             |
| `&17`  | `ReturnHalftone`               | Read the halftone screen.                                                                        |                                                                                                 | R0 to R7 (R0 is 0 if none)                  |
| `&18`  | `SetHalftoneOrigin`            | Set the halftone origin.                                                                         | R0 x, R1 y (graphics coordinates)                                                               |                                             |
| `&19`  | `ReturnHalftoneOrigin`         | Read the halftone origin.                                                                        |                                                                                                 | R0 x, R1 y (pixels)                         |
| `&1A`  | `SelectHalftoneTable`          | Build a table of grey levels for the colours of a mode.                                          | R0 mode, R1 palette, R4 buffer                                                                  | Grey level of each entry                    |
| `&1B`  | `ReturnHalftoneIntensity`      | Return the grey level of a colour.                                                               | R0 colour                                                                                       | R0 grey level 0 to 255                      |
| `&1C`  | `ReturnHalftoneTable`          | Return the grey levels for a range of colours.                                                   | R0 first colour, R1 last colour, R2 buffer (256 bytes)                                          | Grey levels of a ramp                       |
| `&1D`  | `SetScreen`                    | Build a threshold table from a spot function, angle and size.                                    | R0 spot function, R1 angle, R2 x size, R3 y size, R4 argument, R5 low colour, R6 high colour    | Threshold table built                       |
| `&1E`  | `CacheScreen`                  | Return the cached screen bitmap for a key, building it if needed.                                | R0 key                                                                                          | R0 bitmap, R1 length                        |
| `&1F`  | `SelectColourPatternTable`     | Build dither patterns for every palette entry of a mode.                                         | R0 mode, R1 palette, R4 buffer (32 bytes per palette entry)                                     | Patterns written                            |
| `&3C`  | `ReadDitherState` (hidden)     | Read the dither state.                                                                           |                                                                                                 | R0 state                                    |
| `&3D`  | `SuspendDither` (hidden)       | Stop the next call being passed on to ColourV.                                                   |                                                                                                 | Next call is not passed on to ColourV       |
| `&3E`  | `EnableDither` (hidden)        | Enable dithering.                                                                                |                                                                                                 |                                             |
| `&3F`  | `DisableDither` (hidden)       | Disable dithering.                                                                               |                                                                                                 |                                             |

The module also provides the `*Dither [<option>]` command. Option `0` selects the default dither, `1` disables dithering, `2` selects greyscale dither and `4` selects the alternative four colour dither.

`SetScreen` takes either a built-in spot function (`-1` to `-6`) or the address of a user routine in R0. The user routine receives x in R0 and y in R1 and returns its result in R2.

## The disassembly

`Asm/DitherExt.s` is the source of truth for the port. Repeated entry and exit sequences are written with the `EnterSWI`, `ExitOK` and `ExitErr` macros. STM and LDM instructions use register ranges.

Build it with `asasm` and compare the output with the original module. The two files should be identical.

The Antialias entry code at `Antialias` is still raw `DCD` words. It is real code, not data.

## The C port

Every SWI is ported. The port needs the GCCSDK cross compiler (`arm-unknown-riscos-gcc`) and `cmunge`. From `C`:

```
make
```

This produces `DitherExt,ffa`. Run `make clean` to remove `build/` and the module.

### Layout

| File                | Contents                                                                  |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cmhg/DitherExtHdr` | CMHG header: SWI chunk, names and handlers                                |
| `src/main.c`        | Initialisation, SWI dispatch, the simple SWIs and cache freeing           |
| `src/stubs.c`       | SWI dispatch table                                                        |
| `src/dither.h`      | `Workspace` layout (matches the original offsets), SWI numbers and errors |
| `src/colour.c`      | Colour number and GCOL SWIs, palette search, nearest-colour routines      |
| `src/select.c`      | `SelectTable` family                                                      |
| `src/misc.c`        | `ReadPalette`, halftone intensity and table, colour pattern array         |
| `src/pattern.c`     | `SetGCOL`, `SetOppGCOL` and the colour pattern SWIs                       |
| `src/screen.c`      | `CacheScreen`                                                             |
| `src/setscreen.c`   | `SetScreen`: spot functions, trigonometry and the 16 bit divide           |
| `src/antialias.c`   | `Antialias`: chooses a blender for the current depth                      |
| `src/blend.c`       | The eight blenders (2, 4, 8 and 16 and 32 bits per pixel)                 |
| `src/veneer.s`      | Register convention veneers for the blenders                              |
| `src/tables*.c`     | Constant tables extracted from the binary                                 |

### Antialias blenders

`Antialias` does not blend. It returns the workspace address in R0 and the address of a blend routine in R1. The caller then invokes that routine with IP = workspace, R1 = mask, R2 = source, R3 = destination and R4 = count. It returns with `LDMFD sp!, {r0-ip, pc}`.

The blenders are written in C. `veneer.s` adapts the register convention. The blenders are called from outside the module with an arbitrary static base, so they use no static data. They reach tables through extra trailing `Workspace` fields set at start-up. This is why every object is built with `-mno-apcs-stack-check`.

### Known differences and quirks

- The original allocates its caches from the RMA. The port uses `malloc` and `calloc`.
- The port keeps the original's behaviour for valid input. Some overruns are not reproduced as such: `blend_4bpp` can run past the buffers if an aligned shortcut word is met with only two pixels left, and unaligned word copies in the 8 bit blenders follow ARM `LDR` rotation, not `memcpy`.
- The error numbers `0x1E4` (no room) and `0x1E6` (SWI not known) are placeholders. The originals have not been checked.
- The port has not been run on RISC OS. Test at least one `Antialias` call per screen depth.

## Verification

Each ported routine was checked by a differential test against the original binary run in a Unicorn ARM emulator (SA1110 model), using random inputs. The tests are not part of this repository. The results at the last run:

- Colour number, GCOL, `SelectTable`, palette and pattern routines: 0 mismatches.
- `SetScreen`: 57 cases and 2000 inputs each for `Sine`, `ScreenSpot` and `Divide16`, 0 mismatches.
- Blenders: 3000 random cases across all eight, 0 mismatches.

Unicorn does not rotate unaligned `LDR` as an ARM610 or StrongARM does. The test harness patches that one instruction in `Blend16bpp`.

antxiko-dunkshot-msx2-patch-readme-md.text:
# Dunk Shot (MSX) — the MSX2 patch against the flicker

*(También disponible [en castellano](README.es.md).)*

An unofficial patch for **Dunk Shot** (HAL Laboratory, 1986), the 32 KB MSX
cartridge. Every player in the game is four sprites and the MSX1 draws four
per line, so the game shares them out and the players flicker. An MSX2 draws
eight per line: this patch takes the game to SCREEN 4 and turns the sharing
off. On an MSX1 the same file plays as the original.

**The website**: https://antxiko.github.io/DunkShot-MSX2-Patch/

| | |
|---|---|
| the patch | `parche/dunkshot_msx2.ips`, 292 bytes |
| bytes changed | 164, in 24 stretches; no pattern moved |
| sprites not drawn per frame | 66.7 (original, MSX1) → 1.7 (patched, MSX2) |
| worst frame | 166 → 22 |
| on an MSX1 | as the original |
| tested | in openMSX (MSX1 and Philips NMS 8250); **not yet on real hardware** |

No ROM is distributed, neither the original nor the patched one: you supply
your own dump (sha256 `a1891e03...`) and the IPS does the rest. The result
must give sha256 `e5e14b0f...`.

## Applying it

With any IPS tool, or as [Getting started](docs/GETTING-STARTED.md) explains.
Then, in openMSX:

```
openmsx -machine Philips_NMS_8250 -cart dunkshot_msx2.rom
```

## Building it

You need Python 3, GNU make, [Pasmo](https://pasmo.speccy.org/) and your dump
as `dunkshot.rom` at the root:

```
make            # listing, reassembly, checks, the patch and the tests
make parche     # only the patch
```

This repository starts from the
[commented disassembly of Dunk Shot](https://github.com/antxiko/DunkShot-disassembly),
with its history, so every address the patch touches can be looked up in
`src/dunkshot.asm`.

## Notice

The game belongs to HAL Laboratory; only the patch, the analysis, the comments
and the tools are here. See [LEGAL-NOTICE.md](LEGAL-NOTICE.md).

shadester-amigamand-iter020-s.text:
; The pixel loop of the fixed-point build, in registers (vbcc spills most of it to the stack, and a call for every pixel
; costs more than the few iterations most pixels need).
;
;   void run_loop(__reg("a0") LONG *a)       a = the block below, the pens of n pixels along a row or column go to dst
;
;   0 cr (Q8.24, of the next pixel)   4 dx   8 ci   12 n   16 maxit   20 check   24 julia
;   28 jr (Q4.28)   32 ji   36 dst   40 lut   44 saved   48 spent   52 count   56 hit   60 di (step of ci)   64 dst step
;
; Each pixel is what view.c's C loop used to do (squares in Q8.24 are the high long of muls.l, z and c in Q4.28):
;   Mandelbrot: |c| > 2 is 1 iteration at once; inside the main cardioid or the period-2 bulb is maxit at once;
;   then  while (i < maxit && zr2 + zi2 <= 4) { zi = (hi(zr*zi) << 5) + ci;  zr = ((zr2 - zi2) << 4) + cr;
;                                               zr2 = hi(zr*zr);  zi2 = hi(zi*zi);  i++ }
;   Julia: z starts at the pixel, c is the constant.
; The pen is lut[i].
;
; With check set, an orbit that comes back within EPS of a saved state (saved at iterations 1, 2, 4, 8, ...) is taken
; to be periodic and counted as inside (Brent). That is a guess, not a proof: fixed point never repeats a state
; exactly, so only a tolerance can find the cycle. It pays on views with low-period components and costs about a
; fifth of the speed where there are none, so the caller switches it off when saved is small against spent.
; saved: iterations it spared, spent: iterations done, count: inside pixels, while it was on.
;
; d2 zr, d3 zi, d4 cr, d5 ci, d6 zr2, a2 zi2, d7 i, a3 maxit, a1 4.0
; checked loop only: a4, a5 saved zr, zi minus EPS; a0 steps since the save, a6 steps to the next save

	machine	68020

EPS	equ	256		; 2^-20 in Q4.28

UPDATE	macro
	move.l	d2,d0
	muls.l	d3,d1:d0
	lsl.l	#5,d1
	add.l	d5,d1
	move.l	d1,d3			; zi = 2*zr*zi + ci
	move.l	d6,d0
	sub.l	a2,d0
	lsl.l	#4,d0
	add.l	d4,d0
	move.l	d0,d2			; zr = zr2 - zi2 + cr
	move.l	d2,d0
	muls.l	d2,d1:d0
	move.l	d1,d6			; zr2
	move.l	d3,d0
	muls.l	d3,d1:d0
	move.l	d1,a2			; zi2
	addq.l	#1,d7
	endm

SAVE	macro
	move.l	d2,d0
	sub.l	#EPS,d0
	move.l	d0,a4
	move.l	d3,d0
	sub.l	#EPS,d0
	move.l	d0,a5
	endm

	section	code,code

	public	_run_loop
_run_loop:
	movem.l	d2-d7/a2-a6,-(sp)
	move.l	a0,-(sp)
	tst.l	12(a0)
	ble	.exit

.pixel:
	move.l	(sp),a0
	move.l	(a0),d4			; the pixel, Q8.24
	move.l	8(a0),d5
	clr.l	56(a0)
	tst.l	24(a0)
	bne	.julia
	move.l	d4,d0
	add.l	#$02000000,d0
	cmp.l	#$04000000,d0
	bhi	.esc1			; |re| > 2: out after one iteration
	move.l	d5,d0
	add.l	#$02000000,d0
	cmp.l	#$04000000,d0
	bhi	.esc1			; |im| > 2
	cmp.l	#$FE800000,d4		; the cardioid and the bulb lie in -1.5 < re < 0.5, -1 < im < 1
	ble	.noc
	cmp.l	#$00800000,d4
	bge	.noc
	cmp.l	#$FF000000,d5
	ble	.noc
	cmp.l	#$01000000,d5
	bge	.noc
	lsl.l	#4,d4			; to Q4.28: this is c from here on
	lsl.l	#4,d5
	move.l	d5,d0
	muls.l	d5,d1:d0
	move.l	d1,d6			; yy = im^2
	move.l	d4,d0
	sub.l	#$04000000,d0		; xm = re - 1/4
	move.l	d0,a2
	muls.l	d0,d1:d0
	add.l	d6,d1			; q = xm^2 + yy
	move.l	d1,d0
	lsl.l	#4,d0
	move.l	d0,d1
	add.l	a2,d1			; q + xm
	muls.l	d1,d3:d0		; d3 = q * (q + xm)
	move.l	d6,d0
	asr.l	#2,d0
	cmp.l	d0,d3			; inside the cardioid: q * (q + xm) < yy / 4
	blt	.inmax
	move.l	d4,d0
	add.l	#$10000000,d0		; re + 1
	muls.l	d0,d1:d0
	add.l	d6,d1
	cmp.l	#$00100000,d1		; inside the bulb: (re + 1)^2 + yy < 1/16
	blt	.inmax
	moveq	#0,d2
	moveq	#0,d3
	bra.s	.core
.noc:
	lsl.l	#4,d4
	lsl.l	#4,d5
	moveq	#0,d2
	moveq	#0,d3
	bra.s	.core
.julia:
	move.l	d4,d2
	lsl.l	#4,d2			; z is the pixel
	move.l	d5,d3
	lsl.l	#4,d3
	move.l	28(a0),d4		; c is the constant
	move.l	32(a0),d5

.core:
	move.l	16(a0),a3
	move.l	20(a0),a6		; check, until the loop starts
	move.l	#$04000000,a1
	moveq	#0,d7
	move.l	d2,d0
	muls.l	d2,d1:d0
	move.l	d1,d6
	move.l	d3,d0
	muls.l	d3,d1:d0
	move.l	d1,a2
	cmp.l	a3,d7
	bge	.store
	move.l	d6,d0
	add.l	a2,d0
	cmp.l	a1,d0
	bgt	.store
	move.l	a6,d0
	bne.s	.checked

.plain:
	UPDATE
	cmp.l	a3,d7
	bge	.store
	move.l	d6,d0
	add.l	a2,d0
	cmp.l	a1,d0
	ble.s	.plain
	bra	.store

.checked:
	SAVE
	suba.l	a0,a0
	moveq	#1,d0
	move.l	d0,a6
.cloop:
	UPDATE
	move.l	d2,d0
	sub.l	a4,d0
	cmp.l	#2*EPS,d0
	bcc.s	.nochk
	move.l	d3,d0
	sub.l	a5,d0
	cmp.l	#2*EPS,d0
	bcs.s	.hit
.nochk:
	addq.l	#1,a0
	cmpa.l	a6,a0
	bne.s	.cnext
	SAVE
	adda.l	a6,a6
	suba.l	a0,a0
.cnext:
	cmp.l	a3,d7
	bge	.store
	move.l	d6,d0
	add.l	a2,d0
	cmp.l	a1,d0
	ble.s	.cloop
	bra	.store

.hit:
	move.l	(sp),a0
	move.l	d7,56(a0)		; the iteration where the cycle was seen
	move.l	a3,d7			; counted as inside
	bra	.store

.esc1:
	moveq	#1,d7
	bra.s	.store
.inmax:
	move.l	(sp),a0
	move.l	16(a0),d7

.store:
	move.l	(sp),a0
	tst.l	20(a0)
	beq.s	.nostat
	move.l	56(a0),d0
	beq.s	.nohit
	move.l	16(a0),d1
	sub.l	d0,d1
	add.l	d1,44(a0)		; saved += maxit - hit
	add.l	d0,48(a0)		; spent += hit
	addq.l	#1,52(a0)
	bra.s	.nostat
.nohit:
	add.l	d7,48(a0)
	cmp.l	16(a0),d7
	blt.s	.nostat
	addq.l	#1,52(a0)
.nostat:
	move.l	40(a0),a1
	move.b	(a1,d7.l),d0
	move.l	36(a0),a1
	move.b	d0,(a1)
	adda.l	64(a0),a1
	move.l	a1,36(a0)
	move.l	4(a0),d0
	add.l	d0,(a0)			; the next pixel: re and im step, dst steps
	move.l	60(a0),d0
	add.l	d0,8(a0)
	subq.l	#1,12(a0)
	bgt	.pixel
.exit:
	addq.l	#4,sp
	movem.l	(sp)+,d2-d7/a2-a6
	rts

HBT2			DC.W 	'	 BT <$address1> <$address2> eg: BT $908 $90B<CR>',0
HLEN22		  DC.W	 HLEN22-HBT2
HBS1	  		DC.W 	'BS : Searches A Literal String In The Memory',0
HLEN23		  DC.W	 HLEN23-HBS1
HBS2	 		DC.W 	'	 BS <$address1> <$address2> "literal string" eg: BS $900 $910 "MATCH"<CR>',0
HLEN24		  DC.W	 HLEN24-HBS2
HHD1			DC.W 	'HD : Converts A Hex Number To A Dec Number',0
HLEN25		  DC.W	 HLEN25-HHD1
HHD2			DC.W 	'	 HD <hex number> eg: HD $40<CR>',0
HLEN26		  DC.W	 HLEN26-HHD2
HQMD			DC.W 	'QMD: Quickly Displays memory(one byte at a time)<QMD $ADDRESS> eg: QMD $40<CR>',0
HLEN27		  DC.W	 HLEN27-HQMD
HST1			DC.W	'ST : Sorts byte sized data in memory location (both ascending and descending)',0
HLEN28		  DC.W	HLEN28-HST1
HST2			DC.W	'	 <ST $starting address> <$end address> eg: ST $5000 $5010<CR>',0
HLEN29		  DC.W	HLEN29-HST2


******************REGISTERS TABLE*****************************

RSR		DC.W	'SR',0
RD0		DC.W	'D0',0
RD1		DC.W	'D1',0
RD2		DC.W	'D2',0
RD3		DC.W	'D3',0
RD4		DC.W	'D4',0
RD5		DC.W	'D5',0
RD6		DC.W	'D6',0
RD7		DC.W	'D7',0
RA0		DC.W	'A0',0
RA1		DC.W	'A1',0
RA2		DC.W	'A2',0
RA3		DC.W	'A3',0
RA4		DC.W	'A4',0
RA5		DC.W	'A5',0
RA6		DC.W	'A6',0
RA7		DC.W	'A7',0

REG_LEN  DC.W   RSR-RD0

***********************Exception Display Messages**********

BSER		DC.B 'Bus Error Exception',0
ER_LENG1	DC.B  ER_LENG1-BSER
ADER		DC.B 'Address Error Exception',0
ER_LENG2	DC.B  ER_LENG2-ADER
ILER		DC.B 'Illegal Instruction Exception',0
ER_LENG3	DC.B  ER_LENG3-ILER
D0ER		DC.B 'Divide by Zero Exception',0
ER_LENG4	DC.B  ER_LENG4-D0ER
PRER		DC.B 'Priviledge Violation Exception',0
ER_LENG5	DC.B  ER_LENG5-PRER
LFER		DC.B 'Line F Emulator',0
ER_LENG6	DC.B  ER_LENG6-LFER
LAER		DC.B 'Line A Emulator',0
ER_LENG7	DC.B  ER_LENG7-LAER

*************************************************************

	ORG	$2000

START:				  ; first instruction of program
**************************************************************

**************************************************************
*Initialize Vetor Table


	MOVE.L #STACK,$0
	MOVE.L #BUS_ERR,$8
	MOVE.L #ADS_ERR,$C
	MOVE.L #IL_INST,$10
	MOVE.L #DIV_Z,$14
	MOVE.L #PRI_VIO,$20
	MOVE.L #LINE_A,$2C
	MOVE.L #LINE_F,$28


	LEA	 BGN_MSG,A1		   ;LOAD TERMINAL PROMPT
	MOVE.W  #BGN_SIZE,D1		 ;STORE LENGTH OF PROMPT
	MOVEQ.L #1,D0				;OUTPUT TO TERMINAL
	TRAP #15
	BSR NEW_LINE
	BSR NEW_LINE

******************MAIN PROGRAM*******************************
MAIN
	LEA	 PROMPT,A1		   ;LOAD TERMINAL PROMPT
	MOVE.W  #PR_LEN,D1		  ;STORE LENGTH OF PROMPT
	MOVEQ.L #1,D0			   ;OUTPUT TO TERMINAL
	TRAP #15


	BSR	 INIT_BUF
	BSR	 CMD
	BSR	 NEW_LINE
	BRA	 MAIN

**************************************************************
*;Exception Handlers

;Bus
BUS_ERR
			JSR NEW_LINE
			LEA BSER,A1
			MOVE.L  #ER_LENG1,D1
   			MOVE.L  #0,D0
			TRAP #15
	   		JSR NEW_LINE
			JSR DR
			JSR NEW_LINE
			BRA MAIN
			RTS
;ADDRESS
ADS_ERR
			JSR NEW_LINE
			LEA ADER,A1
			MOVE.L  #ER_LENG2,D1
   			MOVE.L  #0,D0
			TRAP #15
			JSR NEW_LINE
			JSR DR
			JSR NEW_LINE
			BRA MAIN
			RTE
;ILLEGAL INSTRUCTION
IL_INST
			JSR NEW_LINE
			LEA ILER,A1
			MOVE.L  #ER_LENG3,D1
   			MOVE.L  #0,D0
			TRAP #15
			JSR NEW_LINE
			JSR DR
			JSR NEW_LINE
			BRA MAIN
			RTS
;DIVIDE BY ZERO
DIV_Z		JSR NEW_LINE
			LEA D0ER,A1
			MOVE.L  #ER_LENG4,D1
   			MOVE.L  #0,D0
			TRAP #15

			JSR NEW_LINE
			JSR DR
			JSR NEW_LINE
			BRA MAIN
			RTS
;PRIVILEDGE VIOLATION
PRI_VIO		JSR NEW_LINE
			LEA PRER,A1
			MOVE.L  #ER_LENG5,D1
   			MOVE.L  #0,D0
			TRAP #15

			JSR NEW_LINE
			JSR DR
			JSR NEW_LINE
			BRA MAIN
			RTS
;LINE F
LINE_F		JSR NEW_LINE
			LEA LAER,A1
			MOVE.L  #ER_LENG6,D1
   			MOVE.L  #0,D0
			TRAP #15

			JSR NEW_LINE
			JSR DR
			JSR NEW_LINE
			BRA MAIN
			RTS

;LINE A
LINE_A		JSR NEW_LINE
			LEA LFER,A1
			MOVE.L  #ER_LENG7,D1
   			MOVE.L  #0,D0
			TRAP #15

			JSR NEW_LINE
			JSR DR
			JSR NEW_LINE
			BRA MAIN
			RTS


******************COMMAND INTERPRETER************************

*PARSE INPUT COMMAND AND STORE IN COMMAND BUFFER*
CMD
	MOVEM.L	D1-D7/A1-A6,-(A7)   ;SAVE REGISTERS
	LEA	 INPUT,A1			;INPUT BUFFER. TRAP 2 READS THE INPUT AND SAVES IT IN A1 AND ITS LENGTH IN D1.
	MOVEQ.L #2,D0			   ;INPUT COMMAND IN INPUT BUFFER
	TRAP #15					;INPUT COMMAND LENGTH IN D1

	CMP.L   #1,D1			   ;CONT. IF COMMAND LENGTH > 1
	BLE	 CMD_ERR_MSG		 ;ELSE, PRINT ERROR MSG

	LEA	 INPUT,A0
	LEA	 COMMAND,A2
	CLR.L   D3
PARSE_LOOP
	MOVE.B  (A0)+,D2
	CMP.B   #SP,D2			  ;IF SPACE, DISREGARD
	BEQ	 LEAD_SPC
	MOVE.B  D2,(A2)+			;STORE NEXT LETTER IN COMMAND BUFFER
	CMP.B   #CR,D2			  ;IF CARRIAGE RETURN, START COMPARING
	BEQ	 COMP_CMD
	ADDI.L  #1,D3			   ;LETTER COUNT

	BRA	 PARSE_LOOP		  ;LOOP UNTIL REACHES CARRIAGE RETURN
LEAD_SPC
	CMP.B   #0,D3			   ;IF LEADING SPACE, RETURN TO PARSE FOLLOWING LETTERS
	BEQ	 PARSE_LOOP		  ;ELSE, CONTINUE ON TO COMPARE

*COMPARE INPUT COMMAND TO COMMAND LIST*
COMP_CMD
	LEA	 CMD_TABL,A1
	LEA	 CMD_ADDR,A2
	LEA	 COMMAND,A3
	MOVE.L  #TABL_LEN,D3		;COMMAND LIST LENGTH
	CLR.L   D6				  ;LOOP COUNTER
	MOVE.L  #5,D7			   ;COMMAND LIST INCREMENTOR
MATCH_LOOP
	ADDI.L  #1,D6
	MOVE.B  (A1)+,D4
	MOVE.B  (A3)+,D5
	CMP.B   #CR,D5			  ;CHECK IF END OF INPUT COMMAND
	BEQ	 MATCH_END		   ;IF NOT END, COMPARE NEXT LETTER
	CMP.B   #SP,D5
	BEQ	 MATCH_END
	CMP.B   D4,D5			   ;COMPARE INPUT COMMAND TO COMMAND LIST
	BEQ	 MATCH_LOOP		  ;IF EQUAL, COMPARE NEXT LETTER
	SUBI.L  #1,D6
	CMPI.L  #1,D6
	BEQ	 NEXT_CMD
	CLR.L   D6
NEXT_CMD
	SUBQ.L  #1,D3			   ;CHECK IF END OF COMMAND LIST
	BEQ	 CMD_ERR_MSG		 ;IF END, THEN INVALID COMMAND
	SUB.L   D6,D7
	ADDA.L  D7,A1			   ;ELSE INCREMENT COMMAND LIST POINTER
	ADDA.L  #2,A2			   ;AND COMMAND ADDRESS POINTER
	LEA	 COMMAND,A3		  ;AND RESET POINTER TO BEGINNING OF COMMAND BUFFER
	CLR.L   D6
	MOVE.L  #5,D7
	BRA	 MATCH_LOOP		  ;LOOP UNTIL MATCH FOUND OR END OF COMMAND LIST
MATCH_END
	MOVE.B  #SP,D5
	CMP.B   D4,D5			   ;CHECK IF COMMAND IN LIST ALSO AT END
	BNE	 CMD_ERR_MSG		 ;IF NOT, THEN INVALID COMMAND
MATCH
	MOVE.L  #0,A4			   ;CLEAR A4
	MOVE.W  (A2),A4			 ;STORE COMMAND SUBROUTINE ADDRESS, A4 has the address of the selected command
	JMP	 (A4)				;JUMP TO COMMAND SUBROUTINE


***********************COMMAND SUBROUTINES*******************************
HE
	LEA	 HHE,A1			  ;HE HELP
	MOVE.L  #HLEN1,D1
	MOVE.L  #0,D0
	TRAP #15

	LEA	 HEX,A1			  ;EX HELP
	MOVE.L  #HLEN2,D1
	TRAP #15

	LEA	 HGO1,A1			 ;GO HELP
	MOVE.L  #HLEN3,D1

MD							  ;FORMAT: MD <$ADDRESS1> <$ADDRESS2>
								;DISPLAYS CONTENTS OF MEMORY FROM ADDR1 TO ADDR2-1

	CLR.L   D5
	CLR.L   D0

	MOVEA.L #0,A2
	MOVEA.L #0,A3

	BSR	 PARSE_ADDR1
	CMP.L   #0,D3			   ;CHECK ERROR FLAG
	BNE	 ARG_ERR_MSG
	BSR	 ASCII_TO_HEX		;CONVERT ADDR1 TO HEX, CONVERSION IN D5
	MOVEA.L D5,A2			   ;SAVE ADDR1
ADR2
	MOVE.B  (A6)+,D2
	CMP.B   #'$',D2			 ;CHECK IF ARG2 STARTS WITH $
	BNE	 ARG_ERR_MSG		 ;IF NOT, ERROR
	MOVEA.L A6,A0			   ;INPUT TO ASCII_TO_HEX
	BSR	 ASCII_TO_HEX
	MOVEA.L D5,A3			   ;SAVE ADDR2

MD_OUTPUT					   ;OUPUT FORMAT: 'CURRENT ADDR   CONTENTS OF CURRENT ADDR'
								;OUTPUTTING CURRENT ADDR...

	CMPA.L  A2,A3			   ;IF CURRENT ADDR=ADDR2, THEN DONE
	BLE	 MD_END
	MOVE.L  A2,D5			   ;INPUT FOR HEX_TO_ASCII
	MOVE.L  #2,D0			   ;ARG FOR HEX_TO_ASCII INDICATING INPUT IS WORD
	BSR	 HEX_TO_ASCII
	BSR	 SPACE			   ;ADD TWO SPACES BEFORE OUTPUTTING
	BSR	 SPACE			   ;CONTENTS OF CURRENT ADDR
								;THE CODE ABOVE IS FOR PRINTING THE ADDRESS(WORD). EX: $5000  . THE BLOCK OF CODE BELOW IS FOR CONTENT (BYTE). EX: $5000  12

	CLR.L   D5				  ;OUTPUTTING CONTENTS OF CURRENT ADDR...
	MOVE.B  (A2)+,D5			;INPUT FOR HEX_TO_ASCII
	MOVEQ.L #1,D0			   ;ARG FOR HEX_TO_ASCII INDICATING INPUT IS BYTE
	BSR	 HEX_TO_ASCII
	BSR	 NEW_LINE			;ADD NEW LINE BEFORE OUTPUTTING
	BRA	 MD_OUTPUT

MD_END
	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D1-D7/A1-A6   ;RESTORE REGISTERS
	RTS

	CLR.L   D5				  ;OUTPUTTING CONTENTS OF CURRENT ADDR...
	MOVE.B  (A2)+,D5			;INPUT FOR HEX_TO_ASCII

	BNE	 ARG_ERR_MSG

ADDR2
	MOVE.B  (A6)+,D2
	CMP.B   #'$',D2			 ;CHECK IF ARG2 STARTS WITH $
	BNE	 ARG_ERR_MSG		 ;IF NOT, ERROR
	MOVEA.L A6,A0			   ;INPUT TO ASCII_TO_HEX
	BSR	 ASCII_TO_HEX
	MOVEA.L D5,A3			   ;SAVE ADDR2
SORT
								;Sorts the data of a specified block byte by byte.
								;No registers are modified by this program.
								;STARTING ADDRESS IN A2 AND ENDING IN A3
	MOVEA.L  A3,A4			  ;A4 IS THE END OF THE UNSORTED PART
BIG_LOOP:
	MOVEA.L  A2,A5			  ;A5 IS THE BUBBLE
SMALL_LOOP:
	MOVE.B  (A5),D2
	ADDA.L  #1,A5
	MOVE.B  (A5),D3
	SUBA.L  #1,A5
	CMP.B   D2,D3
	BGE	 END_SMALL_LOOP
	MOVE.B  D3,(A5)
	ADDA.L  #1,A5
	MOVE.B  D2,(A5)
	SUBA.L  #1,A5
END_SMALL_LOOP:
	ADDA.L  #1,A5
	CMP.L   A5,A4
	BNE	 SMALL_LOOP
END_BIG_LOOP:
	SUBA.L  #1,A4
	CMP.L   A4,A2
	BNE	 BIG_LOOP

	MOVEM.L (SP)+,D0-D7/A0-A6
	BSR NEW_LINE
	BSR MAIN
	RTS

MM							  ;FORMAT: MM <$ADDRESS>
								;BY DEFAULT DISPLAYS ONE BYTE AT A TIME
								;OPTIONS: ;W DISPLAYS WORD AND ;L DISPLAYS LONG
								;CHANGES CONTENTS AT MEM LOC
	CLR.L   D5

	BSR	 PARSE_ADDR1
	CMP.L   #0,D3			   ;CHECK ERROR FLAG
	BNE	 ARG_ERR_MSG
	BSR	 ASCII_TO_HEX		;CONVERT ADDR1 TO HEX, CONVERSION IN D5
	MOVEA.L D5,A2			   ;SAVE ADDR1
	MOVEA.L A6,A1			   ;COPY INPUT
	MOVEA.L A2,A3			   ;COPY ADDR1

	CMP.B   #1,D7			   ;CHECK IF WORD OR LONG OPTION GIVEN
	BNE	 MM_LOOP
	MOVE.B  (A1)+,D2
	CMP.B   #'W',D2
	BEQ	 MM_WORD
	CMP.B   #'L',D2
	BEQ	 MM_LONG
MM_WORD
	MOVE.B  #1,D3
	BRA	 MM_LOOP
MM_LONG
	MOVE.B  #2,D3
MM_LOOP
	MOVE.L  A2,D5
	MOVEQ.L #2,D0
	BSR	 HEX_TO_ASCII		;CONVERT ADDR TO ASCII AND OUPUT
	BSR	 SPACE
	BSR	 SPACE			   ;BY NOW WE HAVE THE ADDRESS THAT WE WANT TO MODIFY DISPLAYED+2 SPACES EX: $5000

	CMP.B   #1,D3			   ;CHECK IF WORD OR LONG OPTION GIVEN
	BEQ	 MM_OUT_WORD
	CMP.B   #2,D3
	BEQ	 MM_OUT_LONG
	MOVE.B  (A2)+,D5			; MOVING THE CONTENT OF THE INPUT ADDRESS TO D5 AS THE INPUT FOR HEX_TO_ASCII IS D5
	MOVE.L  #1,D0
	BRA	 MM_FINAL_OUT
MM_OUT_WORD
	MOVE.W  (A2)+,D5
	MOVE.L  #2,D0
	BRA	 MM_FINAL_OUT
MM_OUT_LONG
	MOVE.L  (A2)+,D5
	CLR.L   D0
MM_FINAL_OUT
	BSR	 HEX_TO_ASCII		;OUPUT CONTENTS OF ADDR IN ASCII.BY NOW WE HAVE THE ADDRESS THAT WE WANT TO MODIFY DISPLAYED+2 SPACES AND ITS CONTENT. EX: $5000  12

	BSR	 SPACE			   ;WITH APPROPRIATE LENGTH (B,W,L)
	MOVE.L  #'?',D1
	MOVE.L  #6,D0
	TRAP #15					;BY NOW WE HAVE THE ADDRESS THAT WE WANT TO MODIFY DISPLAYED+2 SPACES AND ITS CONTENT+'?". EX: $5000  12 ?

MODIFY
	BSR	 INIT_BUF			;TAKE INPUT OF NEW CONTENTS OF ADDR
	LEA	 INPUT,A1
	MOVE.B  #2,D0
	TRAP #15					;THE MEMORY HAS BEEN UPDATED WITH THE NEW VALUE


	MOVEA.L #INPUT,A5		   ;COPY INPUT
	CMP.B   #'.',(A5)		   ;EXIT WITH PERIOD (.) IT MUST BE INPUTTED
	BEQ	 MM_END			  ;BY ITSELF NOT AT END OF LAST MODIFY
	CMP.B   #CR,(A5)			;IF CR CONTINUE TO NEXT ADDR
	BEQ	 MM_LOOP

	MOVEA.L A5,A0			   ;LOAD INPUT TO ASCII_TO_HEX
	BSR	 ASCII_TO_HEX
	MOVEA.L A2,A0			   ;MOVE POINTER BACK TO END OF PREVIOUS ADDR
	CMP.B   #1,D3
	BEQ	 STORE_WORD
	CMP.B   #2,D3
	BEQ	 STORE_LONG
	MOVE.B  D5,(A3)+
	BRA	 MM_LOOP			 ;CONTINUE TO NEXT ADDR
STORE_WORD
	MOVE.W  D5,(A3)
	BRA	 MM_LOOP			 ;CONTINUE TO NEXT ADDR
STORE_LONG
	MOVE.W  D5,(A3)
	BRA	 MM_LOOP			 ;CONTINUE TO NEXT ADDR

MM_END
	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D1-D7/A1-A6   ;RESTORE REGISTERS
	RTS

BF_LOOP

BS							  ;FORMAT: BS <$address1> <$address2> "literal string"
								;SEARCH ADDR1-ADDR2 FOR THE STRING
	BSR	 PARSE_ADDR1		 ;ARG1

	BNE	 ARG_ERR_MSG

	BSR	 ASCII_TO_HEX		;OUTPUT RECEIVED IN D5
	MOVEA.L D5,A3

	BEQ	 ARG_ERR_MSG

BS_LOOP

	CMP.B   (A2)+,D5			;CHECK IF CURRENT ADDR HAS LITERAL STRING
	BEQ	 BS_PASS			 ;IF SO PRINT SUCCESS MSG AND END
	BRA	 BS_LOOP

BS_PASS
	LEA	 BS_PASS_MSG,A1	  ;BS PASSED MSG
	MOVE.W  #BT_LEN3,D1
*	MOVEQ.L #1,D0

	MOVEQ.L #0,D0

BS_FAIL

HD							  ;FORMAT: HD <hex number>
								;SEARCH ADDR1-ADDR2 FOR THE STRING
	CLR.L   D6
	CLR.L   D7
	CLR.L   D2
	CLR.L   D1

	BSR	 PARSE_ADDR1		 ;GET ARG IN ASCII
	CMP.L   #0,D3			   ;CHECK ERROR FLAG
	BNE	 ARG_ERR_MSG
	BSR	 ASCII_TO_HEX		;CONVERT TO HEX, OUTPUT IN D5

HD_LOOP
	DIVU	#10,D5
	SWAP.W  D5
	CMP.W   #0,D5			   ;IF REMAINDER 0, DONE
	BEQ	 HD_OUTPUT
	MOVE.B  D5,D6
	;ANDI.L  #$10,D6			 ;D6 HOLDS REMAINDER
	;CLR.W   D5
	;SWAP.W  D5				  ;D5 HOLDS QUOTIENT
	;BSR	 HD_LOOP2

	LSL.L   D7,D6			   ;SHIFT IN SECOND LOOP
	ADD.B   D6,D2			   ;SAVE TO FINAL ANSWER
	CLR.W   D5				  ;CLEAR REMAINDER
	SWAP.W  D5				  ;GET QUOTIENT IN LOWER WORD
	ADD.B   #4,D7
	BRA	 HD_LOOP

;HD_LOOP2
 ;   CMPI.W  #0,D1
  ;  BEQ	 HD_LOOP1
  ;  MULU	#16,D6
  ;  MOVE.B  D6,D2			   ;SAVE TO FINAL ANSWER
  ;  SUBQ.L  #1,D1
;HD_LOOP3
  ;  CMPI.W  #0,D1
 ;   BEQ	 HD_OUTPUT
   ; MULU	#16,D6
   ; MOVE.B  D6,D2			   ;SAVE TO FINAL ANSWER
	;SUBQ.L  #1,D1

HD_OUTPUT

	BSR HEX_TO_ASCII

HD_END
	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D1-D7/A1-A6   ;RESTORE REGISTERS
	RTS

*************************INITIALIZE POINTERS******************************
INIT_BUF						;CLEAR INPUT AND COMMAND BUFFER
	MOVEM.L	D1-D7/A1-A6,-(A7)
	MOVE.L  #9,D2			   ;LOOP COUNTER
	LEA	 INPUT,A2
IN_LOOP
	MOVE.B  #' ',(A2)+		  ;FILL BUFFER WITH SPACES
	DBRA	D2,IN_LOOP		  ;DECREMENT COUNTER AND REPEAT IF NOT = -1
INIT_CMDBUF					 ;CLEAR COMMAND BUFFER
	MOVE.L  #9,D2			   ;LOOP COUNTER
	LEA	 COMMAND,A2
CMD_LOOP
	MOVE.B  #' ',(A2)+		  ;FILL BUFFER WITH SPACES
	DBRA	D2,CMD_LOOP		 ;DECREMENT COUNTER AND REPEAT IF NOT = -1
	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D1-D7/A1-A6   ;RESTORE REGISTERS
	RTS

*************************ADDRESS PARSING**********************************
PARSE_ADDR1
	MOVEM.L D2,-(A7)			;SAVE REGISTER
	CLR.L   D2
	CLR.L   D3
	CLR.L   D7
	MOVE.B  (A0)+,D2			;
	CMP.B   #'$',D2			 ;CHECK IF ARG1 STARTS WITH $
	BNE	 ADDR_ERR			;IF NOT, ERROR
	MOVEA.L A0,A6			   ;COPY INPUT SO THAT START OF ARG1 SAVED IN A6
ARG_LOOP
	MOVE.B  (A6)+,D2			;READ NEXT CHARACTER
	CMP.B   #SP,D2			  ;CHECK IF END OF ARG1
	BEQ	 ARG_END			 ;IF END, STORE ADDR1
	CMP.B   #CR,D2			  ;CHECK IF END OF INPUT
	BEQ	 ARG_END			 ;IF END, CHECK IF 2 ARGS PROVIDED
	CMP.B   #';',D2
	BEQ	 SET_FLAG			;SET FLAG INDICATES THAT MM OPTIONS PROVIDED
	BRA	 ARG_LOOP
SET_FLAG
	MOVEQ.L #1,D7
	BRA	 ARG_END
ADDR_ERR
	MOVEQ.L #1,D3			   ;WHEN PARSE_ADDRESS IS CALLED AND EXECUTED, THE BIT IN D3 SETS THE FLAG FOR ERROR. HENCE AT EACH COMMAND, WE CHECK D3 AND IF IT IS SET WE PRINT ERRORS.
ARG_END
	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D2			;RESTORE REGISTER
	RTS


**********************CONVERT ASCII TO HEX********************************
ASCII_TO_HEX					;TAKES INPUT IN A0, OUPUT TO D5
	MOVEM.L D4,-(A7)			;SAVE REGISTER
	CLR.L   D4				  ;HOLDS CONVERSION AFTER EACH LOOP
	CLR.L   D5				  ;HOLDS FINAL CONVERSION
ASCII_LOOP
	LSL.L   #4,D5			   ;SHIFT ANSWER TO CLR LAST LOOP ANSWER
	MOVE.B  (A0),D4
	CMP.B   #$39,D4			 ;CHECK IF LETTER OR NUMBER
	BGT	 ASCII_LETTER
	ANDI.B  #$0F,D4			 ;IF NUMBER, MASK ALL BITS EXCEPT LOWEST 4 (SUBTRACTS 30)
	BRA	 CHECK_END
ASCII_LETTER
	SUBI.B  #55,D4
CHECK_END
	ADD.L   D4,D5			   ;ADD TO FINAL CONVERSION
	ADDA.L  #1,A0			   ;INCREMENT TO NEXT CHARACTER
	CMP.B   #SP,(A0)			;CHECK IF END OF INPUT
	BEQ	 ASCII_END
	CMP.B   #CR,(A0)
	BEQ	 ASCII_END
	BRA	 ASCII_LOOP
ASCII_END
	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D4			;RESTORE REGISTER
	RTS

**********************CONVERT HEX TO ASCII********************************
HEX_TO_ASCII					;TAKES INPUT IN D5, OUTPUT TO (A4)
								;D0=1 IF INPUT IS BYTE, D0=2 IF WORD, ELSE LONG
	MOVEM.L D3-D4,-(A7)		 ;SAVE REGISTER
	CLR.L   D3				  ;HOLDS LOOP COUNTER
	CLR.L   D4				  ;HOLDS CONVERSION AFTER EACH LOOP
	MOVEA.L #$3124,A4		   ;HOLDS FINAL CONVERSION
	CMP.B   #1,D0
	BEQ	 HEX_BYTE
	CMP.B   #2,D0
	BEQ	 HEX_WORD
HEX_LONG
	MOVE.L  #7,D3			   ;LOOP COUNTER FOR LONG INPUT
	BRA	 HEX_LOOP
HEX_WORD
	MOVE.L  #3,D3			   ;LOOP COUNTER FOR WORD INPUT
	BRA	 HEX_LOOP
HEX_BYTE
	MOVE.B  #1,D3			   ;LOOP COUNTER FOR BYTE INPUT
HEX_LOOP
	MOVE.B  D5,D4			   ;COPY INPUT
	ANDI.B  #$0F,D4			 ;MASK ALL BITS EXCEPT LOWEST 4
	CMP.B   #9,D4			   ;CHECK IF LETTER OR NUMBER
	BGT	 HEX_LETTER
	ADDI.B  #$30,D4			 ;IF NUMBER, ADD 30 TO CONVERT
	BRA	 HEX_CHECK_END
HEX_LETTER
	ADDI.B  #55,D4
HEX_CHECK_END
	MOVE.B  D4,-(A4)			;ADD TO FINAL CONVERSION
	LSR.L   #4,D5			   ;SHIFT INPUT TO ACCESS NEXT 4 BITS
	DBRA	D3,HEX_LOOP		 ;DECREMENT LOOP COUNTER
HEX_END
	BSR	 OUT_ASCII		   ;OUTPUT FINAL CONVERSION
	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D3-D4		 ;RESTORE REGISTER
	RTS


*************************OUTPUT REGISTERS*********************************
								;OUTPUTS THE CONTENT OF REGISTERS. SR IS ON 1ST LINE, R0,R1,R2 AND R3 ON THE SECOND LINE,FOLLOWED BY R4,R5,R6 AND R7 AND  SO ON.
OUTPUT_REG
	LEA	 RSR,A1			  ;DISPLAY SR
	BSR	 STR_OUT			 ;OUTPUTS SR
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL		   ;PRINTS "=". SO AFTER THIS STEP WE HAVE SR=
	MOVE	SR,D5			   ;MOVES THE CONTENT OF SR TO D5
	BSR	 OUT_WORD			;THE LENGHT OF SR IS WORD. SO AFTER THIS STEP WE HAVE SR= "CONTENT OF SR". EX SR=2000
	BSR	 NEW_LINE			;INSERTS A NEW LINE

	LEA	 RD0,A1			  ;DISPLAY D0
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  D0,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 SPACE

	LEA	 RD1,A1			  ;DISPLAY D1
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  D1,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 SPACE

	LEA	 RD2,A1			  ;DISPLAY D2
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  D2,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 SPACE

	LEA	 RD3,A1			  ;DISPLAY D3
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  D3,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 NEW_LINE

	LEA	 RD4,A1			  ;DISPLAY D4
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  D4,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 SPACE

	LEA	 RD5,A1			  ;DISPLAY D5
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 SPACE

	LEA	 RD6,A1			  ;DISPLAY D6
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  D6,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 SPACE

	LEA	 RD7,A1			  ;DISPLAY D7
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  D7,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 NEW_LINE

	LEA	 RA0,A1			  ;DISPLAY A0
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  A0,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 SPACE

	LEA	 RA1,A1			  ;DISPLAY A1
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  A1,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 SPACE

	LEA	 RA2,A1			  ;DISPLAY A2
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  A2,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 SPACE

	LEA	 RA3,A1			  ;DISPLAY A3
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  A3,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 NEW_LINE

	LEA	 RA4,A1			  ;DISPLAY A4
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  A4,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 SPACE

	LEA	 RA5,A1			  ;DISPLAY A5
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  A5,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 SPACE

	LEA	 RA6,A1			  ;DISPLAY A6
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  A6,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 SPACE

	LEA	 RA7,A1			  ;DISPLAY A7
	BSR	 STR_OUT
	BSR	 OUT_EQUAL
	MOVE.L  A7,D5
	BSR	 OUT_LONG
	BSR	 NEW_LINE

	RTS

OUT_WORD						;DISPLAY WORD
	MOVEM.L D0-D7/A0-A7,-(A7)   ;SAVE REGISTERS
	MOVEQ.L #2,D0			   ;INPUT IS WORD
	BSR	 HEX_TO_ASCII
	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D0-D7/A0-A7
	RTS
OUT_LONG						;DISPLAY LONG
	MOVEM.L D0-D7/A0-A7,-(A7)   ;SAVE REGISTERS
	CLR.L   D0				  ;INPUT IS LONG
	BSR	 HEX_TO_ASCII
	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D0-D7/A0-A7
	RTS

******************************OUPUT ASCII CHARACTERS**********************
OUT_ASCII					   ;TO DISPLAY OUTPUT AFTER HEX_TO_ASCII
	MOVEA.L #$3124,A5
	SUBA.L  A4,A5			   ;CURRENT ADDR LENGTH
	MOVEA.L A4,A1			   ;LOAD CURRENT ADDR FOR OUTPUT
	MOVE.L  A5,D1			   ;LOAD LENGTH OF CURRENT ADDR
	MOVEQ.L #1,D0			   ;OUTPUT TO TERMINAL
	TRAP #15					;RESTORE REGISTER
	RTS

**************************************************************************
STR_OUT						 ;OUTPUT STRING WITHOUT CR LF
	MOVEM.L D0-D7/A0-A7,-(A7)   ;SAVE REGISTERS
	MOVE.L  REG_LEN,D1		  ;STORE LENGTH OF ONE REG OUTPUT
	MOVE.B  #1,D0
	TRAP #15
	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D0-D7/A0-A7   ;RESTORE REGISTER
	RTS

*************************OUTPUT SPACE*************************************
SPACE
	MOVEM.L D0-D1,-(A7)		 ;SAVE REGISTERS

	MOVE.B  #SP,D1			  ;OUTPUT SP
	MOVE.B  #6,D0
	TRAP #15

	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D0-D1		 ;RESTORE REGISTER
	RTS

************************OUTPUT NEW LINE***********************************
NEW_LINE
	MOVEM.L D0-D1,-(A7)		 ;SAVE REGISTERS

	MOVE.B  #13,D1			  ;OUTPUT CR
	MOVE.B  #6,D0
	TRAP #15

	MOVE.B  #10,D1			  ;OUTPUT LF
	MOVE.B  #6,D0
	TRAP #15

	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D0-D1		 ;RESTORE REGISTER
	RTS

**************************OUTPUT EQUAL SIGN*******************************
OUT_EQUAL					   ;DISPLAY EQUAL SIGN
	MOVEM.L D0-D7/A0-A7,-(A7)   ;SAVE REGISTERS
	MOVE.L	#'=',D1
	MOVE.L  #6,D0
	TRAP #15
	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D0-D7/A0-A7   ;RESTORE REGISTER
	RTS

***********************INVALID COMMAND MSG********************************
CMD_ERR_MSG
	LEA	 CMD_ERR,A1		  ;INVALID COMMAND MSG
	MOVE.W  ERR_LEN2,D1		 ;STORE LENGTH OF ERROR MSG
	MOVEQ.L #0,D0			   ;OUTPUT TO TERMINAL
	TRAP #15
	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D1-D7/A1-A6   ;RESTORE REGISTERS
	RTS						 ;DISPLAY PROMPT AGAIN FOR NEXT COMMAND

************************INVALID ARGUMENTS MSG*****************************
ARG_ERR_MSG
	LEA	 ARG_ERR,A1		  ;INVALID ARG MSG
	MOVE.W  ERR_LEN2,D1		 ;STORE LENGTH OF ERROR MSG
	MOVEQ.L #0,D0			   ;OUTPUT TO TERMINAL
	TRAP #15
	MOVEM.L (A7)+,D1-D7/A1-A6   ;RESTORE REGISTERS
	RTS						 ;DISPLAY PROMPT AGAIN FOR NEXT COMMAND

***************************************************************************
	ORG $4000


	CLR.W D0			;ADRESS ERROR
	MOVE.W $1234,$5001

	ORG $4050
	MOVE.B #0,D1		;DIVIDE BY ZERO ERROR
	MOVE.B #5,D2
	DIVU	D1,D2

	ORG $4100		   ;PRIVILEDGE VIOLATION
	ANDI.W #$0700,SR
	BRA $4100

	ORG $4150
	MOVE.B $FFFFFF,D7
	BRA MAIN

	ORG $4200
	MOVE.L  #$123456,D2
	MOVE.B  #$AA,D0
	MOVE.L  #$5555,A2
	BRA MAIN

    ORG $900
		
		*cause an address error
		MOVE.B #9,D0
		TRAP #14
		MOVE.B #9,D0
		TRAP #15





	END	START		; last line of source

antxiko-dunkshot-msx2-patch-parche-parch.text:
; ---- gancho_inigrp ----
    org 0xBFD4
gancho_inigrp:
    call 0x0072          ; INIGRP: SCREEN 2 con la BIOS, como antes
    ld hl,0x3E00         ; ATRBAS: la tabla de atributos visible, 0x3E00
    ld (0xF928),hl
    ld a,(0x002D)        ; version del MSX: 0 = MSX1
    and a
    ld bc,0x7C05         ; R5 = 0x7C: atributos en 0x3E00 (TMS9918)
    jp z,0x0047          ; MSX1: WRTVDP y vuelve
    ld bc,0x0400         ; R0 = 0000 0100: M4 -> G3 (SCREEN 4)
    call 0x0047          ; WRTVDP, deja RG0SAV al dia
    ld bc,0x7F05         ; R5 = 0x7F: el bloque de 1 KB de 0x3C00, bits 0-2 a 1
    jp 0x0047

; ---- r5_segun_maquina ----
    org 0xBFF3
r5_segun_maquina:        ; B = 0x7C o 0x7E (la alternancia del MSX1), C = 5
    ld a,(0x002D)        ; version del MSX
    and a
    jr z,escribe         ; MSX1: tal cual
    ld b,0x7F            ; MSX2: siempre el mismo bloque, 0x3E00 a la vista
escribe:
    jp 0x0047            ; WRTVDP

; ---- tabla_colores ----
    org 0x6EA0
tabla_colores:           ; HL = el color del sprite 0 en una lista de atributos en RAM
    ld a,(0x002D)        ; version del MSX
    and a
    ret z                ; MSX1: no hay tabla de colores de sprite
    di
    push hl
    ld hl,0x3C00         ; la tabla de colores de sprite: la primera mitad del bloque de R5
    call 0x0053          ; SETWRT
    pop hl
    ld a,(0x0007)        ; el puerto de datos del VDP
    ld c,a
    ld d,32              ; los 32 sprites
bucle:
    ld a,(hl)            ; su color, con el bit 7 (EC) si lo lleva
    and 0x8F             ; sin los bits CC e IC del modo 2
    ld b,16
lineas:
    out (c),a            ; el mismo color en las 16 lineas
    djnz lineas
    inc hl
    inc hl
    inc hl
    inc hl               ; el siguiente atributo
    dec d
    jr nz,bucle
    ei
    ret

; ---- fin_tabla ----
    org 0x6EC9
fin_tabla:               ; HL = la entrada de atributos donde acaba la lista
    ld a,0xD0            ; Y = 208: fin de tabla en el TMS9918
    call 0x5AF7          ; escribe_vram: A en la VRAM HL
    inc hl
    inc hl
    inc hl
    inc hl
    ld a,0xD8            ; Y = 216: fin de tabla en el V9938 (modo 2)
    jp 0x5AF7

; ---- colores_menu ----
    org 0x6F30
colores_menu:            ; el final de viste_jugador: su bucle y luego los colores
    dec b
    jp nz,0x80B8         ; los cuatro atributos de la figura
    ld hl,0x3E00         ; los 8 atributos de las dos figuras, de la VRAM
    ld de,0xE730         ; a la lista de la otra tabla (el partido la rehace)
    ld bc,0x0020
    call 0x5B2A          ; lee_de_vram
    ld hl,0xE733         ; el color del sprite 0
    jp 0x6EA0            ; tabla_colores

; ---- vuelca_colores ----
    org 0x7AAE
vuelca_colores:          ; el final de vuelca_sprites: la segunda copia y los colores
    call 0x5B07          ; copia_a_vram: la lista a 0x3F00, como antes
    ld hl,0xE7B3         ; el color del sprite 0 de la lista rotada, la que se ve en MSX2
    jp 0x6EA0            ; tabla_colores

			PalCol&(NC) = VAL("&H" + B$ + G$ + R$)
			PRINT TAB(5); "           R G B: "; R$; "."; G$; "."; B$
		NEXT

		PRINT "Trovato -> CAMG"
		ViewMode$ = ""
		FOR i = 0 TO 7

		NEXT

		NumData$ = ""
		FOR i = 0 TO 3

		NEXT
		nCol% = Wid% / 8
		PRINT TAB(5); "     NumByteData: "; NumData$
		NumData& = VAL("&H" + NumData$)
		DIM DatB%(nPlanes%, nCol% + 1)
		Bl& = 0
		IF Compression% = 1 THEN
			SCREEN 13
'      WINDOW SCREEN (0, 0)-(Wid%, Height%)
			FOR NC = 0 TO NumCol% - 1
				PALETTE NC, PalCol&(NC)
			NEXT
'      PALETTE 1, &H2F2F2F
'      COLOR 1
			FOR Linea = 1 TO Height%
'        PRINT "Linea:"; Linea,
				FOR BitPlane = 0 TO nPlanes% - 1
					Colonna = 0
					DO
						N = ASC(INPUT$(1, 1))
						Bl& = Bl& + 1
						IF N < 128 THEN
							FOR i = 0 TO N
								DatB%(BitPlane, Colonna) = ASC(INPUT$(1, 1))
								Bl& = Bl& + 1
								Colonna = Colonna + 1
							NEXT
						ELSE
							DatB%(BitPlane, Colonna) = ASC(INPUT$(1, 1))
							Bl& = Bl& + 1
							FOR i = 1 TO 256 - N
								DatB%(BitPlane, Colonna + i) = DatB%(BitPlane, Colonna)
							NEXT
							Colonna = Colonna + 256 - N + 1
						END IF
					LOOP UNTIL Colonna = nCol%
				NEXT
				yscr = Linea - 1
				FOR Colonna = 0 TO nCol% - 1
					xscr = Colonna * 8
					IF xscr < 640 AND Linea < 480 THEN
						FOR i = 0 TO 7
							iand = 2 ^ i
							Colore% = 1 * SGN(DatB%(0, Colonna) AND iand)
							Colore% = Colore% + 2 * SGN(DatB%(1, Colonna) AND iand)
							Colore% = Colore% + 4 * SGN(DatB%(2, Colonna) AND iand)
							Colore% = Colore% + 8 * SGN(DatB%(3, Colonna) AND iand)
							IF nPlane% > 4 THEN
								Colore% = Colore% + 16 * SGN(DatB%(4, Colonna) AND iand)
							END IF
							PSET (xscr + 8 - i, yscr), Colore%
						NEXT
					END IF
				NEXT
'        PRINT Bl
			NEXT
		ELSE
		END IF
		EXIT DO
	END SELECT
LOOP

CLOSE #1

    Opensource library with functions for use Sprites from V9938 using

       https://github.com/mvac7/SDCC_VDP_TMS9918A_MSXROM_Lib
    
    For SDCC 3.9 or higher. 
    
  History of versions:
    v0.9 (28/3/2021)                   
============================================================================= */ 

#include "../include/VDP_SPRITES_mode2.h"

#include "../include/msxSystemVars.h"
#include "../include/msxBIOS.h"


#define YHIDDEN  217


char SPRITE_YBUFF[32];




/* =============================================================================
 ClearSprites
 Description: 
             Initialises all sprite data The sprite pattern is cleared to
             null, the sprite number to the sprite plane number, the
             sprite colour to the foregtound colour. The vertical location
             of the sprite is set to 209 (mode 0 to 3) or 217 (mode 4 to 8).
 Input:       -
 Output:      -
============================================================================= */
void ClearSprites() __naked
{
__asm
  push IX
  call CLRSPR
  pop  IX
  ret
__endasm;
}    



/* =============================================================================
 PUTSPRITE
 Description: Displays the sprite pattern.
              In G4 screen mode (V9938), fills the 16 rows of color values.
 Input:       [char] sprite plane (0-31) 
              [char] x 
              [char] y
              [char] pattern
 Output:      -
============================================================================= */
void PUTSPRITE(char plane, char x, char y, char pattern) __naked
{
plane;x;y;pattern;
__asm
  push IX
  ld   IX,#0
  add  IX,SP

  ld   A,4(IX) ;num sprite plane
  call CALATR ;get the VRAM address of the sprite attribute table
  
  ld   B,A
  ld   A,6(IX) ;y
  call WRITEY
  
  inc  HL  
  ld   A,5(IX) ;x
  call WRTVRM
  
  inc  HL  
  ld   E,7(IX)
  call SPRPATNOV  ;pattern
    
  pop  IX
  ret

__endasm;
}



/* =============================================================================
 SetSpritePattern
 Description: Assign a pattern to a sprite plane.
 Input:       [char] sprite plane (0-31) 
              [char] pattern
 Output:      -
============================================================================= */
void SetSpritePattern(char plane, char pattern) __naked
{
plane;pattern; 
__asm
  push IX
  ld   IX,#0
  add  IX,SP
  
  ld   A,4(ix) ;num sprite plane  
  call CALATR  ;get the VRAM address of the sprite attribute table
  inc  HL
  inc  HL
  
  ld   E,5(ix) ;number of pattern to assign  
  call SPRPATNOV
  
  pop  IX
  ret
  


; set sprite pattern number
; Multiply * 4 when its a 16x16 sprite.
; E - Sprite Number  
SPRPATNOV:  ;sprite pattern no calc vram address
  call GSPSIZ          ;0x008A get sprite size in bytes 
  cp   #32             ;16x16
  jr   NZ,WRTPAT

  ;si es 16x16
  SLA  E
  SLA  E ;multiplica x4  

WRTPAT:
  LD   A,E
  jp   WRTVRM
  
__endasm;
}



/* =============================================================================
 SetSpriteColor
 Description: Assign a color to a sprite plane.
              In G4 screen mode (V9938), fills the 16 rows of color values.
 Input:       [char] sprite plane (0-31) 
              [char] color (0-15)
 Output:      -
============================================================================= */
/*void SetSpriteColor(char plane, char color) __naked
{
plane;color;
__asm
  push IX
  ld   IX,#0
  add  IX,SP

  ld   A,4(IX) ;num sprite plane
;  ld   E,5(IX) ;color

;  ld   A,D
;  push DE  
  call getVRAMcolorspr
;  pop  DE
  
  ld   A,5(IX) ;color
  ld   BC,#16
  call FILVRM
  
  pop  IX
  ret

__endasm;
}*/



/* =============================================================================
 SetSpritePosition
 Description: Assigns the position coordinates of a sprite plane.
 Input:       [char] sprite plane (0-31) 
              [char] x 
              [char] y
 Output:      -
============================================================================= */
void SetSpritePosition(char plane, char x, char y) __naked
{
plane;x;y;
__asm
  push IX
  ld   IX,#0
  add  IX,SP
  
  ld   A,4(ix) ;num sprite
  call CALATR  ;get in HL the VRAM address of the sprite attribute table
  
  ld   B,A
  ld   A,6(ix)   ;y
  call WRITEY
  
  inc  HL
  ld   A,5(ix)   ;x
  call WRTVRM
  
  pop  IX
  ret
  
WRITEY:
  ld   IY,#_SPRITE_YBUFF
  ld   D,#0
  ld   E,B
  ADD  IY,DE  
  ld   (IY),A        ; save Y position
  jp   WRTVRM  
   
__endasm;
}



/* =============================================================================
 SetSpriteVisible
 Description: Hides or shows a sprite plane.
 Input:       [char] sprite plane (0-31) 
              [boolean] visible state
 Output:      -
============================================================================= */
void SetSpriteVisible(char plane, boolean state) __naked
{
plane;state;
__asm
  push IX
  ld   IX,#0
  add  IX,SP
  
  ld   A,4(ix) ;num sprite
  
  ld   IY,#_SPRITE_YBUFF
  ld   D,#0
  ld   E,A
  ADD  IY,DE
  
  call CALATR   ;get in HL the VRAM address of the sprite attribute table

  ld   A,5(ix) ;state
  or   A ;0 = off
  jr   Z,SPRITEOFF
  
;sprite ON
  ld   A,(IY)  ;get Y value
  
  call WRTVRM
    
  pop  IX
  ret


;sprite OFF
SPRITEOFF:
  call RDVRM
  cp   #YHIDDEN
  jr   Z,ENDOFF ;if not visible then Dont overwrite. 

  ld   A,#YHIDDEN
  call WRTVRM
  
ENDOFF:
  pop  IX
  ret
__endasm;
}



/* =============================================================================
 SetEarlyClock
 Description: Apply the Early Clock of a sprite. Move 32 points to the left           
              the X position of the sprite.
 Input:       [char] sprite plane (0-31) 
 Output:      -
============================================================================= */
void SetEarlyClock(char plane) __naked
{
plane;
__asm
  push IX
  ld   IX,#0
  add  IX,SP
  
  ld   A,4(IX)  
  call getVRAMcolorspr
  
  ld   B,#16
nextSetEC:
  push HL
  call NRDVRM   ;VPEEK V9938
  OR   #128
  pop  HL
  call WRTVRM   ;VPOKE V9938
  inc  HL  
  djnz nextSetEC

  pop  IX
  ret
  
__endasm;
}



/* =============================================================================
 UnsetEarlyClock
 Description: Disables the Early Clock. Restore the position of a sprite.
 Input:       [char] sprite plane (0-31)
 Output:      -
============================================================================= */
void UnsetEarlyClock(char plane) __naked
{
plane;
__asm
  push IX
  ld   IX,#0
  add  IX,SP

  ld   A,4(IX)
  call getVRAMcolorspr
  
  ld   B,#16
nextUnsetEC:
  call NRDVRM   ;VPEEK V9938
  and  #127
  call WRTVRM   ;VPOKE V9938
  inc  HL 
  djnz nextUnsetEC
  
  pop  IX
  ret




;ASM FUNCTIONS <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<

; >A - sprite plane
; <HL - VRAM addr
getVRAMcolorspr:
  ld   HL,#0x1C00    ;vram address color table base (screen 4)
  ld   D,#0          
  ld   E,A
  SLA  E             ;multiplico A por 16 para identificar la posicion en la VRAM
  RL   D             ;con cuatro rotaciones
  SLA  E
  RL   D
  SLA  E
  RL   D
  SLA  E
  RL   D
  add  HL,DE  
   
  ret
  
__endasm;
}
